chapters.title: Chapter 1 · John the Baptizer; Jesus Begins in Galilee
chapters.intro: The story opens in the wilderness: a man named John is baptizing people in the Jordan River and saying that someone stronger than he is about to come. Jesus is baptized, is tested in the wilderness, and then goes back north to Galilee announcing that the kingdom of God has come near. He calls four fishermen to follow him, drives an unclean spirit out of a man in the synagogue at Capernaum, heals Simon’s mother-in-law and many others, and finally heals a man with a skin disease. “He” in the first verses is John; from verse 9 on it is mostly Jesus.

verses.en: The beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ.

cmp.note: 和合本这里多「神的儿子」几个字。许多古抄本有这几个字（huiou theou），也有几份重要的古抄本没有；本站的底本取了没有的读法，所以白话和英文里都没有。
cmp.en: The 1919 Chinese Union Version adds 神的儿子 (Shén de érzi, "the Son of God") here. Many ancient manuscripts have the words (huiou theou) and a few important ones lack them; the edition this site follows prints the shorter reading, so neither translation has them.

verses.en: As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: “Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way;

cmp.note: 经文说引的是以赛亚，其实这一节的引文出自旧约的《玛拉基书》3:1（并《出埃及记》23:20），下一节才出自《以赛亚书》40:3。较晚的抄本把这里改成了「先知们的书上」。
cmp.en: The text names Isaiah, but the words quoted in this verse come from Malachi 3:1 (with Exodus 23:20); only the next verse is from Isaiah 40:3. Later manuscripts changed the phrase to "in the prophets."

verses.en: a voice of one calling out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight,’”
John the baptizer appeared in the wilderness, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
And the whole Judean countryside and all the people of Jerusalem were going out to him, and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
And John was clothed in camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
And he proclaimed, saying, “After me comes one who is stronger than I; I am not fit to stoop down and untie the strap of his sandals.
I baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.”
And it happened in those days that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized in the Jordan by John.
And immediately, as he was coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens being torn open and the Spirit coming down on him like a dove.

cmp.note: 原文是「被撕开」，很用力的一个词，和合本作「裂开了」。同一个动词在这卷书快结尾的地方（15:38）再出现一次：圣殿里的幔子从上到下裂成两半。
cmp.en: The Greek is "being torn apart," a forceful word; the Union Version has 裂开了 (lièkāi le, "split open"). The same verb returns near the end of the book (15:38), when the curtain of the temple is torn in two from top to bottom.

verses.en: And a voice came from the heavens: “You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased.”
And immediately the Spirit drives him out into the wilderness.

cmp.note: 原文是「赶出去」，和后面「赶鬼」是同一个动词，而且用的是现在时；和合本作「催」，语气轻一些。
cmp.en: The Greek is "throws out," the same verb used below for casting out demons, and it is in the present tense; the Union Version softens it to 催 (cuī, "urged").

verses.en: And he was in the wilderness forty days, being tested by Satan; and he was with the wild animals, and the angels were attending him.
And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the good news of God

cmp.note: 原文是「被交出去」，没有说交给谁；和合本直接写成「下监」。这个动词后面还要用在耶稣自己身上（9:31、14:10：他被交到人手里）。
cmp.en: The Greek is "was handed over," without saying to whom; the Union Version writes 下监 (xià jiān, "put in prison"). The same verb is later used of Jesus himself (9:31; 14:10).

verses.en: and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent and believe in the good news.”
And passing along by the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew, Simon’s brother, casting nets in the sea, for they were fishermen.
And Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you become fishers of people.”
And immediately they left the nets and followed him.
And going on a little farther, he saw James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, who were in the boat mending the nets,
and immediately he called them. And leaving their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men, they went off after him.
And they go into Capernaum; and immediately on the Sabbath he was teaching in the synagogue.
And they were astonished at his teaching, for he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
And immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
saying, “What have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: the Holy One of God.”

cmp.note: 字面是「对我们、对你，有什么？」，是从希伯来话来的说法，意思是「我们和你各不相干，你别来管我们」。
cmp.en: Literally "What to us and to you?", an idiom carried over from Hebrew meaning "we have nothing to do with each other; leave us alone."

verses.en: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent, and come out of him.”
And the unclean spirit, convulsing him and crying out with a loud voice, came out of him.
And they were all amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, “What is this? A new teaching! With authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him.”
And the report about him went out immediately everywhere, into the whole surrounding region of Galilee.
And immediately, having come out of the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
Now Simon’s mother-in-law was lying down with a fever, and immediately they tell him about her.
And he came and raised her up, taking her by the hand; and the fever left her, and she began to serve them.
And when evening came, when the sun had set, they were bringing to him all who were sick and those possessed by demons.
And the whole town was gathered at the door.
And he healed many who were sick with various diseases, and cast out many demons; and he would not let the demons speak, because they knew him.
And very early, while it was still dark, he got up and went out, and went off to a deserted place, and there he was praying.
And Simon and those with him hunted for him,
and they found him and say to him, “Everyone is looking for you.”
And he says to them, “Let us go elsewhere, into the neighboring towns, so that I may proclaim there also; for that is why I came out.”
And he went throughout all Galilee, proclaiming in their synagogues and casting out the demons.
And a man with a skin disease comes to him, begging him and kneeling and saying to him, “If you are willing, you can make me clean.”

cmp.note: 原文 lepra 在当时指好几种皮肤病，不等于今天医学上说的麻风病。按犹太律法（旧约《利未记》13–14 章），得这种病的人算「不洁净」，要离开人群独自住，所以他求的不只是病好，而是「洁净」。
cmp.en: Greek lepra covered several skin conditions and is not the same as what medicine now calls leprosy. Under Jewish law (Leviticus 13–14) a person with it was "unclean" and had to live apart, which is why he asks not just to be healed but to be made "clean."

verses.en: And being angered, he stretched out his hand and touched him, and says to him, “I am willing; be made clean.”

cmp.note: 本站的底本这里是「发怒」（orgistheis）；绝大多数抄本是「动了怜悯的心」（splanchnistheis），和合本的「动了慈心」跟的是后一种。底本取了少数抄本里这个比较难解的读法。耶稣为什么发怒，经文没有说。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "being angered" (orgistheis); the great majority of manuscripts read "moved with compassion" (splanchnistheis), which the Union Version follows with 动了慈心 (dòng le cíxīn, "was moved to pity"). The edition chose the harder reading found in a few manuscripts. The text does not say why he was angry.

verses.en: And immediately the skin disease left him, and he was made clean.
And sternly warning him, he sent him away at once,
and says to him, “See that you say nothing to anyone; but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”

But he went out and began to proclaim it widely and to spread the word, so that he could no longer enter a town openly, but stayed outside in deserted places; and they kept coming to him from everywhere.

chapters.title: Chapter 2 · Forgiving Sins, Eating with Sinners, the Sabbath
chapters.intro: Back in Capernaum, Jesus first tells a paralyzed man his sins are forgiven and then tells him to get up and walk, which the scribes object to. He calls Levi, a tax collector, and eats with tax collectors and sinners. Then come three challenges in a row: why he eats with such people, why his disciples do not fast, and why they pluck grain on the Sabbath. He answers each one.

verses.en: And when he entered Capernaum again after some days, it was heard that he was at home;
and many were gathered, so that there was no longer room, not even at the door, and he was speaking the word to them.
And they come, bringing to him a paralyzed man carried by four.
And not being able to bring him to him because of the crowd, they removed the roof where he was, and having dug through, they let down the mat on which the paralyzed man was lying.
And Jesus, seeing their faith, says to the paralyzed man, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”
Now some of the scribes were sitting there and reasoning in their hearts,
“Why does this man speak like this? He is blaspheming! Who can forgive sins except one, God?”
And immediately Jesus, perceiving in his spirit that they were reasoning this way within themselves, says to them, “Why are you reasoning these things in your hearts?
Which is easier, to say to the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and take your mat and walk’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he says to the paralyzed man,

cmp.note: 字面是「人的儿子」。在希伯来话里这本来就是「人」的意思；旧约《但以理书》7:13 又用它称一位从上帝那里得到权柄的人物。在这卷书里，只有耶稣用它来说自己。
cmp.en: Literally "the son of man." In Hebrew idiom the phrase simply means "a human being," and Daniel 7:13 uses it of a figure who receives authority from God. In this book only Jesus uses it, and always of himself.

verses.en: “I say to you, get up, take your mat and go to your home.”
And he got up and immediately, taking the mat, went out in front of everyone, so that they were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We never saw anything like this.”
And he went out again beside the sea; and all the crowd was coming to him, and he was teaching them.
And passing by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth, and he says to him, “Follow me.” And getting up, he followed him.
And it happens that he is reclining at table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners were reclining with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many, and they were following him.

cmp.note: 原文是「斜躺着」：当时正式的饭局，人是侧身斜靠在垫子上吃的。和合本译「坐席」，白话直接写「吃饭」。
cmp.en: The Greek is "to recline": at a formal meal people lay on their side on cushions. The Union Version has 坐席 (zuòxí, "sat at the feast"); the plain Chinese simply says 吃饭 (chīfàn, "ate").

verses.en: And the scribes of the Pharisees, seeing that he was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, were saying to his disciples, “He eats with the tax collectors and sinners?”
And hearing it, Jesus says to them, “Those who are strong have no need of a doctor, but those who are sick; I did not come to call the righteous but sinners.”
And John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. And they come and say to him, “Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples do not fast?”
And Jesus said to them, “Can the sons of the wedding hall fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

cmp.note: 字面是「婚房的儿子们」，是从希伯来话来的说法，指陪着新郎的亲友宾客。和合本译「陪伴之人」。
cmp.en: Literally "the sons of the wedding hall," a Hebrew-style phrase for the bridegroom’s friends and guests. The Union Version has 陪伴之人 (péibàn zhī rén, "those who accompany").

verses.en: But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast in that day.
No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; otherwise the patch pulls away from it, the new from the old, and a worse tear results.
And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is lost and the skins too. But new wine is for new wineskins.”
And it happened that he was passing through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and his disciples began to make their way, plucking the heads of grain.
And the Pharisees were saying to him, “Look, why are they doing on the Sabbath what is not permitted?”
And he says to them, “Have you never read what David did when he was in need and was hungry, he and those with him:

how he entered the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the loaves of the presentation, which it is not permitted to eat except for the priests, and gave also to those who were with him?”

cmp.note: 这件事记在旧约《撒母耳记上》21 章，那里说当时的祭司是亚希米勒，亚比亚他是他的儿子，后来才作大祭司。
cmp.en: The story is in 1 Samuel 21, where the priest at the time is Ahimelech; Abiathar was his son and became high priest later.

verses.en: And he was saying to them, “The Sabbath came to be for the sake of man, and not man for the sake of the Sabbath;
so the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”

chapters.title: Chapter 3 · The Twelve; Who Are My Mother and Brothers
chapters.intro: Jesus heals a man with a withered hand on the Sabbath, and the Pharisees begin to plot against him. Crowds come from every region; he goes up a mountain and appoints twelve disciples. Scribes say he drives out demons by the ruler of demons, and he answers in parables. Finally his mother and brothers come for him, and he says that whoever does the will of God is his family.

verses.en: And he entered the synagogue again, and a man was there who had a withered hand.
And they were watching him closely, whether he would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse him.
And he says to the man who had the withered hand, “Get up, into the middle.”
And he says to them, “Is it permitted on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to kill?” But they were silent.
And looking around at them with anger, grieved at the hardness of their hearts, he says to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
And the Pharisees went out and immediately were taking counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.
And Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea, and a great multitude from Galilee followed; and from Judea
and from Jerusalem and from Idumea and beyond the Jordan and around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing all that he was doing, came to him.
And he told his disciples to have a small boat ready for him because of the crowd, so that they would not crush him;
for he had healed many, so that all who had afflictions were pressing upon him to touch him.
And the unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, were falling down before him and crying out, saying, “You are the Son of God.”
And he was sternly warning them many times not to make him known.
And he goes up on the mountain and calls to him those whom he himself wanted, and they went to him.
And he appointed twelve, so that they might be with him and so that he might send them out to proclaim
and to have authority to cast out the demons.
And he appointed the twelve: and to Simon he gave the name Peter;

cmp.note: 彼得（Petros）在希腊话里是「石头」的意思。从这里起，这卷书就多半叫他彼得，不再叫西门。
cmp.en: Peter (Petros) means "rock" in Greek. From here on the book mostly calls him Peter rather than Simon.

verses.en: and James the son of Zebedee and John the brother of James, and to them he gave the name Boanerges, that is, Sons of Thunder;
and Andrew and Philip and Bartholomew and Matthew and Thomas and James the son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus and Simon the Cananaean

cmp.note: 这个词来自亚兰话的「热心的人」，不是「迦南人」。和合本照意思译成「奋锐党的」，白话跟和合本；英文照字面写 Cananaean。
cmp.en: The word comes from the Aramaic for "zealous one," not from "Canaanite." The Union Version translates the sense as 奋锐党的 (Fènruìdǎng de, "of the Zealot party"), which the plain Chinese follows; the English keeps the form "Cananaean."

verses.en: and Judas Iscariot, who also handed him over.
And he comes into a house; and the crowd gathers again, so that they were not able even to eat bread.
And when those close to him heard, they went out to seize him, for they were saying, “He is out of his mind.”

cmp.note: 字面是「他那边的人」，多数人理解为他的家里人（第 31 节来的正是他母亲和兄弟），和合本译「亲属」。
cmp.en: Literally "those from beside him," usually taken to be his family (his mother and brothers arrive in verse 31); the Union Version has 亲属 (qīnshǔ, "relatives").

verses.en: And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, “He has Beelzebul,” and, “By the ruler of the demons he casts out the demons.”
And calling them to him, he was speaking to them in parables: “How can Satan cast out Satan?
And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand;
and if a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.
And if Satan has risen up against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but is coming to an end.
But no one can enter the house of the strong man and plunder his goods unless he first binds the strong man, and then he will plunder his house.
Amen I say to you, all things will be forgiven the sons of men, the sins and the blasphemies, whatever they may blaspheme;

cmp.note: 「阿们」是希伯来话，意思是「真的、确实」，平常放在祷告的结尾。耶稣把它放在自己的话前面，表示下面这句话很要紧。和合本译「我实在告诉你们」，白话照用。
cmp.en: "Amen" is Hebrew for "truly, surely," normally said at the end of a prayer. Jesus puts it before his own words to mark what follows as weighty. The Union Version renders it 我实在告诉你们 (wǒ shízài gàosu nǐmen, "I truly tell you"), which the plain Chinese keeps.

verses.en: but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit has no forgiveness forever, but is guilty of an eternal sin.”
For they were saying, “He has an unclean spirit.”
And his mother and his brothers come, and standing outside they sent to him, calling him.
And a crowd was sitting around him, and they say to him, “Look, your mother and your brothers are outside looking for you.”
And answering them he says, “Who is my mother or my brothers?”
And looking around at those sitting in a circle about him, he says, “Here are my mother and my brothers!
For whoever does the will of God, this one is my brother and sister and mother.”

chapters.title: Chapter 4 · The Parable of the Sower; Calming the Storm
chapters.intro: Sitting in a boat, Jesus tells the crowd on the shore the parable of the sower, and later explains it privately to his disciples: the seed is the word, and the four kinds of ground are four kinds of hearers. He adds parables of a lamp, of seed that grows by itself, and of a mustard seed. That evening a storm rises as they cross the lake; he rebukes the wind and the sea, and they grow calm.

verses.en: And again he began to teach beside the sea. And a very large crowd gathers to him, so that he got into a boat and sat in it on the sea, and all the crowd was beside the sea on the land.
And he was teaching them many things in parables, and he was saying to them in his teaching:
“Listen! Look, the sower went out to sow.
And it happened as he sowed that some fell beside the road, and the birds came and ate it up.
And other seed fell on rocky ground where it did not have much soil, and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil;
and when the sun rose it was scorched, and because it had no root it withered.
And other seed fell among the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it, and it gave no fruit.
And others fell into the good soil and were giving fruit, coming up and growing, and they bore thirtyfold and sixtyfold and a hundredfold.”
And he was saying, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”
And when he was alone, those around him with the twelve were asking him about the parables.
And he was saying to them, “To you the mystery of the kingdom of God has been given, but to those outside everything comes in parables,
so that ‘seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest they turn back and it be forgiven them.’”

cmp.note: 单引号里的话引自旧约《以赛亚书》6:9–10，那里是上帝对先知以赛亚说的，讲的是百姓听了也不肯明白。
cmp.en: The words in single quotation marks are taken from Isaiah 6:9–10, where God tells the prophet Isaiah that the people will hear and yet refuse to understand.

verses.en: And he says to them, “Do you not understand this parable? And how will you understand all the parables?
The sower sows the word.
And these are the ones beside the road where the word is sown: when they hear, immediately Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.
And these likewise are the ones sown on the rocky places: when they hear the word, immediately they receive it with joy,
and they have no root in themselves but last only for a time; then, when affliction or persecution comes because of the word, immediately they stumble.
And others are the ones sown among the thorns: these are the ones who have heard the word,
and the cares of the age and the deceit of wealth and the desires for other things come in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
And those are the ones sown on the good soil, who hear the word and accept it and bear fruit, thirtyfold and sixtyfold and a hundredfold.”
And he was saying to them, “Does the lamp come in order to be put under the measuring basket or under the bed? Is it not to be put on the lampstand?
For nothing is hidden except to be made visible, nor has anything become secret but that it might come into the open.
If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”
And he was saying to them, “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you measure it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you.
For whoever has, it will be given to him; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him.”
And he was saying, “The kingdom of God is like this: as if a man should throw seed on the ground
and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should sprout and grow tall, he himself does not know how.
By itself the earth bears fruit: first the blade, then the head, then the full grain in the head.

cmp.note: 原文这个词就是「自己动的、不用人管的」，英文 automatic 从它来。和合本译「出于自然的」。
cmp.en: The Greek word means "self-moving, without anyone’s help" and is the source of English "automatic." The Union Version has 出于自然的 (chū yú zìrán de, "of its own nature").

verses.en: But when the fruit allows, immediately he sends in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”
And he was saying, “How shall we compare the kingdom of God, or in what parable shall we put it?
It is like a mustard seed, which, when it is sown on the ground, is smaller than all the seeds on the earth—
and when it is sown, it comes up and becomes greater than all the garden plants and puts out large branches, so that the birds of the sky can nest under its shade.”
And with many such parables he was speaking the word to them, as they were able to hear;
and without a parable he was not speaking to them, but privately to his own disciples he was explaining everything.
And on that day, when evening had come, he says to them, “Let us go across to the other side.”
And leaving the crowd, they take him along, just as he was, in the boat; and other boats were with him.
And a great storm of wind comes up, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was already filling.
And he himself was in the stern, sleeping on the cushion; and they wake him and say to him, “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?”
And having woken, he rebuked the wind and said to the sea, “Silence! Be still!” And the wind dropped, and there was a great calm.

cmp.note: 这个「住口」和第 1 章第 25 节耶稣斥责污灵时说的是同一个动词，字面是「戴上嘴套」。和合本在那里译「不要作声」，这里译「静了罢」。
cmp.en: This "be still" is the same verb Jesus used to rebuke the unclean spirit in 1:25; literally "be muzzled." The Union Version has 不要作声 (búyào zuòshēng, "make no sound") there and 静了罢 (jìng le ba, "be quiet") here.

verses.en: And he said to them, “Why are you cowardly? Do you not yet have faith?”
And they feared a great fear and were saying to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”

chapters.title: Chapter 5 · Legion and the Pigs; Jairus’s Daughter; the Woman with the Flow of Blood
chapters.intro: On the far side of the lake Jesus drives a host of unclean spirits out of a man who lives among the tombs; they enter a herd of pigs, which rushes into the lake and drowns. Back across, a synagogue leader named Jairus begs him to save his dying daughter; on the way a woman who has bled for twelve years touches his cloak and is healed. The girl has died by the time they arrive, and Jesus tells her to get up.

verses.en: And they came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gerasenes.
And when he had got out of the boat, immediately there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit,
who had his dwelling among the tombs, and no one could bind him any longer, not even with a chain,
because he had often been bound with shackles and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him and the shackles broken in pieces, and no one was strong enough to subdue him.
And all the time, night and day, among the tombs and on the mountains he was crying out and cutting himself with stones.
And seeing Jesus from far off, he ran and bowed down before him,
and crying out with a loud voice he says, “What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, do not torment me.”
For he was saying to him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit.”
And he was asking him, “What is your name?” And he says to him, “Legion is my name, for we are many.”

cmp.note: 这是从拉丁文借来的词，指罗马军队的一个军团，满编有五六千人。和合本译成「群」。
cmp.en: A word borrowed from Latin for a unit of the Roman army, five to six thousand men at full strength. The Union Version translates it 群 (qún, "a crowd").

verses.en: And he was begging him much not to send them out of the region.
Now there was there on the hillside a great herd of pigs feeding;
and they begged him, saying, “Send us to the pigs, so that we may enter them.”
And he permitted them. And the unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea, about two thousand, and they were drowned in the sea.
And those feeding them fled and reported it in the town and in the countryside; and they came to see what it was that had happened.
And they come to Jesus and see the demon-possessed man sitting, clothed and in his right mind, the one who had had the legion, and they were afraid.
And those who had seen it told them how it had happened to the demon-possessed man, and about the pigs.
And they began to beg him to go away from their borders.
And as he was getting into the boat, the man who had been demon-possessed was begging him that he might be with him.
And he did not let him, but says to him, “Go to your home, to your own people, and report to them all that the Lord has done for you, and that he had mercy on you.”
And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis all that Jesus had done for him, and everyone was amazed.
And when Jesus had crossed again in the boat to the other side, a great crowd gathered to him, and he was beside the sea.
And one of the synagogue leaders comes, Jairus by name, and seeing him he falls at his feet
and begs him much, saying, “My little daughter is at the point of death; come and lay your hands on her, so that she may be saved and live.”
And he went away with him. And a great crowd was following him and pressing in on him.
And a woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years,
and had suffered much under many doctors and had spent all that she had and was no better but rather had grown worse,
having heard about Jesus, came in the crowd from behind and touched his cloak;
for she was saying, “If I touch even his clothes, I will be saved.”
And immediately the source of her blood was dried up, and she knew in her body that she was healed of the affliction.
And immediately Jesus, perceiving in himself that power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd and was saying, “Who touched my clothes?”
And his disciples were saying to him, “You see the crowd pressing in on you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
And he was looking around to see the woman who had done this.
But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had happened to her, came and fell down before him and told him the whole truth.
And he said to her, “Daughter, your faith has saved you; go in peace, and be healed of your affliction.”

cmp.note: 希腊文里「救」和「治好」是同一个动词（sōzō）。第 23 节睚鲁说「让她得救」、第 28 节女人说「就会好」，用的都是它；英文三处都写 saved，白话按上下文分开写。
cmp.en: In Greek "save" and "heal" are one verb (sōzō). Jairus in verse 23 and the woman in verse 28 use it too; the English writes "saved" all three times, while the plain Chinese varies with the context.

verses.en: While he was still speaking, they come from the synagogue leader’s house, saying, “Your daughter has died; why trouble the teacher any further?”
But Jesus, overhearing the word being spoken, says to the synagogue leader, “Do not fear, only believe.”

cmp.note: 这个词可以是「从旁听到」，也可以是「听了却不理会」，两种读法都有人取。和合本作「听见」，白话和英文取前一种。
cmp.en: The word can mean "overhearing" or "hearing but paying no heed," and both readings have supporters. The Union Version has 听见 (tīngjiàn, "heard"); the plain Chinese and the English take the first sense.

verses.en: And he did not allow anyone to follow with him except Peter and James and John the brother of James.
And they come to the house of the synagogue leader, and he sees a commotion, and people weeping and wailing loudly,
and entering he says to them, “Why are you making a commotion and weeping? The child has not died but is sleeping.”
And they were laughing at him. But he, having put them all out, takes the father of the child and the mother and those with him, and goes in where the child was.
And taking the child’s hand he says to her, “Talitha koum,” which is translated, “Little girl, I say to you, get up.”

cmp.note: 这是亚兰话，耶稣和当地人平常说的语言。这卷书有几处保留了耶稣的亚兰话原话，再翻成希腊文给读者看。
cmp.en: This is Aramaic, the everyday language of Jesus and the people around him. The book keeps his Aramaic words in a few places and then translates them into Greek for its readers.

verses.en: And immediately the girl got up and was walking, for she was twelve years old. And immediately they were amazed with great amazement.
And he gave them strict orders that no one should know this, and said that something should be given her to eat.

chapters.title: Chapter 6 · Rejected at Home; John Beheaded; Five Loaves and Two Fish
chapters.intro: Jesus goes back to his hometown, where people will not accept him. He sends the twelve out in pairs to proclaim and to cast out demons. The book then goes back to tell how King Herod, bound by an oath, had John the baptizer beheaded. When the twelve return, Jesus feeds five thousand people with five loaves and two fish; that night he comes to the disciples’ boat walking on the lake.

verses.en: And he went out from there and comes into his hometown, and his disciples follow him.

And when the Sabbath came, he began to teach in the synagogue; and many who heard were astonished, saying, “Where did this man get these things, and what is the wisdom given to this man, and such mighty works done through his hands?
Is this not the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon? And are his sisters not here with us?” And they were taking offense at him.
And Jesus was saying to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown and among his relatives and in his own house.”
And he was not able to do any mighty work there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
And he was amazed because of their unbelief. And he was going around the villages in a circle, teaching.
And he calls the twelve to him and began to send them out two by two, and he was giving them authority over the unclean spirits,
and he instructed them to take nothing for the road except a staff only: no bread, no bag, no copper in the belt,
but to wear sandals, and not to put on two tunics.
And he was saying to them, “Wherever you enter a house, stay there until you leave that place.
And whatever place does not receive you and they do not listen to you, as you go out from there shake off the dust under your feet as a testimony against them.”
And going out they proclaimed that people should repent,
and they were casting out many demons, and were anointing with oil many who were sick and healing them.
And King Herod heard, for his name had become known, and they were saying, “John the baptizer has been raised from the dead, and that is why the powers are at work in him.”

cmp.note: 本站的底本是「人们说」（elegon）；多数抄本是「他说」（elegen），也就是希律说，和合本的「就说」跟的是后一种。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "they were saying" (elegon); most manuscripts read "he was saying" (elegen), that is, Herod, which the Union Version follows with 就说 (jiù shuō, "then he said").

verses.en: But others were saying, “He is Elijah,” and others were saying, “A prophet, like one of the prophets.”
But when Herod heard, he was saying, “The one I beheaded, John—he has been raised.”
For Herod himself had sent and seized John and bound him in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother, because he had married her.
For John was saying to Herod, “It is not permitted for you to have your brother’s wife.”
And Herodias held a grudge against him and wanted to kill him, and she could not,
for Herod feared John, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man, and he kept him safe; and when he heard him he was greatly perplexed, and yet he heard him gladly.

cmp.note: 本站的底本是「非常困惑」（polla ēporei）；多数抄本是「做了许多事」（polla epoiei），和合本的「就多照着行」跟的是后一种。两个词只差几个字母。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "was greatly perplexed" (polla ēporei); most manuscripts read "did many things" (polla epoiei), which the Union Version follows with 就多照着行 (jiù duō zhàozhe xíng, "did much accordingly"). The two readings differ by only a few letters.

verses.en: And an opportune day came when Herod on his birthday gave a banquet for his nobles and the military commanders and the leading men of Galilee,
and when the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those reclining with him. The king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
And he swore to her, “Whatever you ask me I will give you, up to half of my kingdom.”
And going out she said to her mother, “What shall I ask for?” And she said, “The head of John the baptizer.”
And coming in immediately with haste to the king, she asked, saying, “I want you to give me at once on a platter the head of John the Baptist.”
And the king became deeply grieved, but because of his oaths and those reclining at table he did not want to refuse her.
And immediately the king sent an executioner and ordered him to bring his head. And he went and beheaded him in the prison
and brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.
And when his disciples heard, they came and took his body and laid it in a tomb.
And the apostles gather to Jesus, and they reported to him all that they had done and all that they had taught.

cmp.note: 「使徒」原文的意思就是「被派出去的人」，和第 7 节「派他们出去」是同一个词根。
cmp.en: "Apostles" in Greek simply means "those sent out," from the same root as "to send them out" in verse 7.

verses.en: And he says to them, “Come away, you yourselves, privately to a deserted place and rest a little.” For those coming and going were many, and they did not even have time to eat.
And they went away in the boat to a deserted place privately.
And many saw them going and recognized them, and they ran there together on foot from all the towns and got there ahead of them.
And when he got out he saw a great crowd, and he was moved with compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things.
And when the hour was already late, his disciples came to him and were saying, “The place is deserted, and the hour is already late;
send them away, so that they may go into the surrounding farms and villages and buy themselves something to eat.”
But answering he said to them, “You give them something to eat.” And they say to him, “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give it to them to eat?”
And he says to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go, see.” And when they knew, they say, “Five, and two fish.”
And he ordered them to have everyone recline, group by group, on the green grass.
And they reclined in plots, by hundreds and by fifties.
And taking the five loaves and the two fish, looking up to heaven he blessed and broke the loaves and was giving them to his disciples to set before them, and the two fish he divided among them all.
And they all ate and were filled;
and they took up broken pieces, twelve baskets full, and also from the fish.
And those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.
And immediately he made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead to the other side, toward Bethsaida, while he himself dismisses the crowd.
And having taken leave of them, he went away to the mountain to pray.
And when evening had come, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the land.
And seeing them straining at the rowing, for the wind was against them, about the fourth watch of the night he comes to them, walking on the sea; and he wanted to pass by them.
But when they saw him walking on the sea, they thought it was a ghost and cried out,
for they all saw him and were terrified. But immediately he spoke with them, and he says to them, “Take courage; it is I; do not be afraid.”
And he got up into the boat with them, and the wind dropped. And they were utterly astounded within themselves,
for they had not understood about the loaves, but their heart was hardened.

cmp.note: 字面是「变硬了、结了茧」，和第 3 章第 5 节耶稣为法利赛人「心硬」难过是同一个词根；这里说的是门徒。和合本译「愚顽」。
cmp.en: Literally "hardened, calloused," from the same root as the "hardness of heart" Jesus grieved over in the Pharisees at 3:5; here it is said of the disciples. The Union Version has 愚顽 (yúwán, "dull and stubborn").

verses.en: And when they had crossed over they came to land at Gennesaret and moored there.
And when they got out of the boat, immediately people recognized him
and ran about that whole region and began to carry around on mats those who were sick, to wherever they heard he was.

And wherever he went, into villages or into towns or into farms, they were laying the sick in the marketplaces and begging him that they might touch even the fringe of his cloak; and as many as touched him were being saved.

cmp.note: 犹太男子按律法在外衣四角缝上穗子，提醒自己记住上帝的诫命（旧约《民数记》15:38）。和合本译「衣裳繸子」。
cmp.en: By the law Jewish men wore tassels on the four corners of the outer garment as a reminder of God’s commandments (Numbers 15:38). The Union Version has 衣裳繸子 (yīshang suìzi, "the tassel of the garment").

chapters.title: Chapter 7 · What Makes a Person Unclean
chapters.intro: Pharisees and scribes challenge Jesus because his disciples eat without the ritual washing of hands. He answers that they use human tradition to cancel God’s commandment, and tells the crowd that what defiles a person is not what goes in but the evil that comes out of the heart. He then travels into Gentile territory, where he drives a demon out of a foreign woman’s daughter and heals a man who is deaf and can hardly speak.

verses.en: And the Pharisees and some of the scribes, having come from Jerusalem, gather around him,
and seeing that some of his disciples were eating their bread with defiled hands, that is, unwashed—

cmp.note: 字面是「普通的手」「俗的手」，说的是按宗教规矩算不洁净，和讲不讲卫生无关。和合本译「俗手」，白话写「不洁净的手」。
cmp.en: Literally "common hands": unclean in the ritual sense, which has nothing to do with hygiene. The Union Version has 俗手 (sú shǒu, "common hands"); the plain Chinese writes 不洁净的手 (bù jiéjìng de shǒu, "unclean hands").

verses.en: for the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands with the fist, holding to the tradition of the elders,

cmp.note: 字面是「用拳头」，确切指哪一种洗法已经不清楚。和合本译「仔细」；白话写成「照规矩」，英文照字面。
cmp.en: Literally "with the fist"; exactly what manner of washing is meant is no longer clear. The Union Version has 仔细 (zǐxì, "carefully"); the plain Chinese writes 照规矩 (zhào guīju, "in the prescribed way"), and the English keeps the literal wording.

verses.en: and when they come from the marketplace they do not eat unless they wash; and there are many other things they have received to hold to, the washing of cups and pitchers and copper vessels and dining couches—
and the Pharisees and the scribes ask him, “Why do your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their bread with defiled hands?”
And he said to them, “Isaiah prophesied well about you hypocrites, as it is written: ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far away from me;

cmp.note: 这一节和下一节引的是旧约《以赛亚书》29:13。
cmp.en: This verse and the next quote Isaiah 29:13.

verses.en: in vain do they worship me, teaching as teachings the commandments of men.’
Leaving the commandment of God, you hold to the tradition of men.”
And he was saying to them, “You do well at setting aside the commandment of God, so that you may keep your tradition.
For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Whoever speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.’

cmp.note: 两句分别出自旧约《出埃及记》20:12 和 21:17。
cmp.en: The two sayings are from Exodus 20:12 and 21:17.

verses.en: But you say, if a man says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever you would have gained from me is Corban,’ that is, a gift,

cmp.note: 希伯来话，指许愿献给上帝的东西。东西一旦说成是各耳板，就不能再拿去给别人用，哪怕是奉养父母。马可照音写下，再用希腊文解释成「礼物」。
cmp.en: A Hebrew word for something vowed to God. Once a thing was declared Corban it could no longer be used for anyone else, even to support one’s parents. Mark writes the sound of the word and then explains it in Greek as "gift."

verses.en: you no longer let him do anything for his father or mother,
making void the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down; and you do many such things like this.”
And calling the crowd to him again, he was saying to them, “Listen to me, all of you, and understand:
there is nothing from outside a person that, going into him, can defile him; but the things that come out of a person are what defile the person.”
(This verse is not in the Greek edition this site follows.)

cmp.note: 较晚的抄本这里有一句话，意思是「谁有耳朵能听，就该听」，和 4:9、4:23 的话一样。最早的几份抄本没有这一句，一般认为是抄写的人照前面的话补进来的，所以底本不收。
cmp.en: Later manuscripts have a sentence here meaning "If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear," the same saying as in 4:9 and 4:23. The earliest manuscripts lack it, and it is generally thought that copyists added it from those earlier passages, so the edition leaves it out.

verses.en: And when he went into a house away from the crowd, his disciples were asking him about the parable.
And he says to them, “Are you also so lacking in understanding? Do you not see that whatever goes into a person from outside cannot defile him,
because it does not go into his heart but into the stomach, and goes out into the latrine?”—making all foods clean.

cmp.note: 字面是「洁净一切食物」，原文只有这几个字，没有写主语。一般读成讲故事的人插进来的一句：耶稣这样说，等于宣布各样食物都洁净。和合本译「这是说，各样的食物都是洁净的」。
cmp.en: Literally "cleansing all foods," with no subject expressed. It is usually read as the narrator’s aside: by saying this Jesus declared all foods clean. The Union Version renders it 这是说、各样的食物、都是洁净的 (zhè shì shuō, gèyàng de shíwù, dōu shì jiéjìng de, "this means that every kind of food is clean").

verses.en: And he was saying, “What comes out of a person, that defiles the person.
For from within, out of the heart of people, come evil thoughts: sexual immoralities, thefts, murders,
adulteries, greeds, wickednesses, deceit, licentiousness, an evil eye, slander, pride, foolishness.

cmp.note: 字面是「恶眼」，犹太人的说法，指眼红别人、小气。白话和和合本都写「嫉妒」，英文照字面。这两节的分节，底本和和合本不一样：和合本把「偷盗、凶杀」放在这一节。
cmp.en: Literally "an evil eye," a Jewish idiom for envy or stinginess. Both Chinese versions write 嫉妒 (jídù, "envy"); the English keeps the literal phrase. The verse division also differs: the Union Version puts "thefts, murders" in this verse.

verses.en: All these evil things come from within and defile the person.”
And from there he got up and went away to the region of Tyre. And entering a house, he wanted no one to know, yet he could not escape notice;
but immediately a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having heard about him, came and fell down at his feet.
Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by birth; and she was asking him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
And he was saying to her, “Let the children be fed first, for it is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the little dogs.”

cmp.note: 原文是「小狗」，指家里养的狗，和合本只写「狗」。一般的理解是：「儿女」指犹太人，「小狗」指外族人。
cmp.en: The Greek is a diminutive, "little dogs," meaning dogs kept in the house; the Union Version writes simply 狗 (gǒu, "dogs"). The usual understanding is that "the children" are the Jews and "the little dogs" the Gentiles.

verses.en: But she answered and says to him, “Lord, even the little dogs under the table eat from the children’s crumbs.”
And he said to her, “Because of this word, go; the demon has gone out of your daughter.”
And going away to her house, she found the child lying on the bed and the demon gone.
And again, going out from the region of Tyre, he came through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee, through the midst of the region of the Decapolis.
And they bring to him a man who was deaf and spoke with difficulty, and they beg him to lay his hand on him.
And taking him aside from the crowd privately, he put his fingers into his ears, and having spat, he touched his tongue,
and looking up to heaven he sighed, and says to him, “Ephphatha,” that is, “Be opened.”

cmp.note: 这是亚兰话，当时犹太人平常说的语言。马可照音写下耶稣的原话，再用希腊文解释意思。
cmp.en: This is Aramaic, the everyday language of Jews at the time. Mark writes down the sound of Jesus’s own word and then gives its meaning in Greek.

verses.en: And his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he was speaking plainly.
And he ordered them to tell no one; but the more he ordered them, the more abundantly they were proclaiming it.
And they were astonished beyond measure, saying, “He has done all things well; he makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak.”

chapters.title: Chapter 8 · “Who Do You Say That I Am?”
chapters.intro: Jesus feeds four thousand people with seven loaves and refuses the Pharisees’ demand for a sign, while the disciples in the boat still fail to understand him. At Bethsaida he heals a blind man in two stages. On the road to Caesarea Philippi Peter says, “You are the Christ,” and Jesus for the first time says plainly that he must suffer, be killed and rise after three days, and that anyone who follows him must take up a cross.

verses.en: In those days, when again there was a large crowd and they had nothing to eat, he called the disciples to him and says to them,
“I have compassion on the crowd, because they have stayed with me three days already and have nothing to eat;
and if I send them away hungry to their homes, they will faint on the way; and some of them have come from far away.”
And his disciples answered him, “From where will anyone be able to satisfy these people with bread here in a desolate place?”
And he was asking them, “How many loaves do you have?” And they said, “Seven.”

And he directs the crowd to recline on the ground; and taking the seven loaves, having given thanks, he broke them and was giving them to his disciples to set before them, and they set them before the crowd.
And they had a few small fish; and having blessed them, he said that these also should be set before them.
And they ate and were satisfied; and they took up the leftover broken pieces, seven baskets.
Now there were about four thousand. And he sent them away.
And immediately, getting into the boat with his disciples, he came to the district of Dalmanutha.

cmp.note: 这个地名在古代文献里只出现这一次，确切在哪里已经不清楚，一般认为在加利利湖的西岸。
cmp.en: This place name occurs only here in ancient literature and its exact location is unknown; it is generally placed on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee.

verses.en: And the Pharisees came out and began to argue with him, seeking from him a sign from heaven, testing him.
And sighing deeply in his spirit, he says, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Truly I say to you, no sign will be given to this generation.”

cmp.note: 字面是「如果有神迹给这一代人……」，后半句不说出来。这是希伯来话里起誓的说法，意思是「绝不会」。白话和英文都直接写出这个意思。
cmp.en: Literally "if a sign shall be given to this generation…," with the rest left unsaid. This is a Hebrew way of swearing an oath and means "certainly not." Both translations give that meaning directly.

verses.en: And leaving them, he got into the boat again and went away to the other side.
And they forgot to take loaves, and except for one loaf they had nothing with them in the boat.
And he was ordering them, saying, “Watch out; beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.”
And they were discussing with one another that they have no loaves.
And knowing it, he says to them, “Why are you discussing that you have no loaves? Do you not yet perceive or understand? Do you have your heart hardened?
Having eyes, do you not see, and having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember,
when I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” They say to him, “Twelve.”
“And when the seven for the four thousand, how many large baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” And they say to him, “Seven.”
And he was saying to them, “Do you not yet understand?”
And they come to Bethsaida. And they bring to him a blind man and beg him to touch him.
And taking hold of the blind man’s hand, he brought him out of the village, and having spat on his eyes and laid his hands on him, he was asking him, “Do you see anything?”
And looking up, he was saying, “I see people, for I see them like trees, walking around.”
Then again he laid his hands on his eyes, and he looked intently and was restored, and he was seeing everything clearly.
And he sent him to his house, saying, “Do not even go into the village.”
And Jesus went out, and his disciples, to the villages of Caesarea Philippi; and on the way he was asking his disciples, saying to them, “Who do people say that I am?”
And they told him, saying, “John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; and others, one of the prophets.”
And he was asking them, “But you, who do you say that I am?” Peter answers and says to him, “You are the Christ.”
And he sternly warned them to tell no one about him.
And he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise;
and he was speaking the word openly. And Peter, taking him aside, began to rebuke him.

cmp.note: 原文是「责备」，和下一节耶稣「责备」彼得、第 30 节「严厉地吩咐」是同一个动词，也是第 1 章里耶稣斥责污灵用的词。和合本这里写成「劝他」，语气轻了。
cmp.en: The Greek is "rebuke," the same verb used in the next verse when Jesus rebukes Peter, in verse 30 ("sternly warned"), and in chapter 1 when Jesus rebukes the unclean spirit. The Union Version softens it here to 劝他 (quàn tā, "urged him").

verses.en: But turning and seeing his disciples, he rebuked Peter and says, “Get behind me, Satan, for you are not thinking the things of God but the things of men.”
And calling the crowd to him with his disciples, he said to them, “If anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever will lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s will save it.

cmp.note: 这个词既指「性命」，也指「灵魂」「自己这个人」。第 35 到 37 节四次用它，耶稣的话正是靠这两层意思：保住了命，可能丢了自己。白话统一写「性命」，和合本写「生命」，英文写 life。
cmp.en: The word means "life" but also "soul" or "one’s very self." It is used four times in verses 35–37, and the saying turns on both senses: one can keep one’s life and lose oneself. The plain Chinese writes 性命 (xìngmìng, "life") throughout, the Union Version 生命 (shēngmìng, "life"), the English "life."

verses.en: For what does it profit a person to gain the whole world and forfeit his life?
For what could a person give in exchange for his life?
For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, of him the Son of Man will also be ashamed when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.”

chapters.title: Chapter 9 · The Transfiguration
chapters.intro: Jesus takes three disciples up a high mountain and is transfigured before them, and a voice from a cloud says, “This is my beloved Son.” Back down, he drives out a spirit the disciples could not, and for the second time foretells that he will be killed and rise after three days. The disciples meanwhile argue about who is greatest; Jesus takes a child in his arms, teaches them to be servants of all, and warns them against causing others to stumble.

verses.en: And he was saying to them, “Truly I say to you, there are some of those standing here who will certainly not taste death until they see the kingdom of God having come in power.”
And after six days Jesus takes Peter and James and John, and brings them up a high mountain privately, alone. And he was transfigured before them,
and his garments became glistening, exceedingly white, such as no launderer on earth is able to whiten them.
And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.
And Peter answers and says to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here; and let us make three tents, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah.”
For he did not know what to answer, for they had become terrified.
And a cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud: “This is my beloved Son; listen to him.”
And suddenly, looking around, they no longer saw anyone but Jesus alone with them.
And as they were coming down from the mountain, he ordered them to tell no one what they had seen, until the Son of Man should rise from the dead.
And they kept the word to themselves, discussing what the rising from the dead is.
And they were asking him, saying, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

cmp.note: 这个说法出自旧约《玛拉基书》4:5：上帝说，在「主的大日子」来到以前，要先派先知以利亚来。
cmp.en: The idea comes from Malachi 4:5, where God says he will send the prophet Elijah before "the great day of the Lord" comes.

verses.en: And he said to them, “Elijah does come first and restores all things; and how is it written of the Son of Man that he should suffer many things and be treated with contempt?
But I say to you that Elijah has indeed come, and they did to him whatever they wished, just as it is written of him.”

cmp.note: 一般认为耶稣这里说的「已经来过的以利亚」指施洗的约翰；第 6 章讲了约翰怎样被希律杀掉。
cmp.en: It is generally understood that the "Elijah who has come" is John the Baptist; chapter 6 tells how Herod had John killed.

verses.en: And coming to the disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.
And immediately all the crowd, seeing him, were greatly amazed, and running up they were greeting him.
And he asked them, “What are you arguing about with them?”
And one out of the crowd answered him, “Teacher, I brought my son to you, who has a mute spirit;
and wherever it seizes him it throws him down, and he foams and grinds his teeth and becomes rigid; and I told your disciples to cast it out, and they were not able.”
And he answers them and says, “O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him to me.”
And they brought him to him. And seeing him, the spirit immediately convulsed him, and falling on the ground he was rolling about, foaming.
And he asked his father, “How long is it that this has been happening to him?” And he said, “From childhood;
and often it has thrown him both into fire and into waters, to destroy him; but if you can do anything, help us, having compassion on us.”
And Jesus said to him, “‘If you can’! All things are possible for the one who believes.”

cmp.note: 底本里耶稣是把那位父亲的话「你要是能」原样重复了一遍。许多抄本这里多一个「信」字，成了「你若能信」，和合本跟的是那一种。
cmp.en: In this edition Jesus simply repeats the father’s own words, "If you can." Many manuscripts add "believe," giving "If you can believe," which the Union Version follows with 你若能信 (nǐ ruò néng xìn, "if you can believe").

verses.en: Immediately the father of the child, crying out, was saying, “I believe; help my unbelief.”
And Jesus, seeing that a crowd is running together, rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, “You mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him and never enter him again.”
And crying out and convulsing him greatly, it came out; and he became like a dead person, so that most of them were saying that he had died.
But Jesus, taking him by the hand, raised him, and he stood up.
And when he had gone into a house, his disciples were asking him privately, “Why were we not able to cast it out?”
And he said to them, “This kind can come out by nothing except by prayer.”
And going out from there, they were passing through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know;
for he was teaching his disciples and saying to them, “The Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of men, and they will kill him; and having been killed, after three days he will rise.”
But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid to ask him.
And they came to Capernaum. And being in the house, he was asking them, “What were you discussing on the way?”
But they were silent, for on the way they had argued with one another about who was greatest.
And sitting down, he called the twelve and says to them, “If anyone wants to be first, he shall be last of all and servant of all.”
And taking a little child, he set him in the midst of them, and taking him in his arms, he said to them,
“Whoever receives one of such little children in my name receives me; and whoever receives me, receives not me but the one who sent me.”
John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we were stopping him, because he was not following us.”
But Jesus said, “Do not stop him, for there is no one who will do a mighty work in my name and be able soon afterward to speak evil of me;
for whoever is not against us is for us.
For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in the name that you are Christ’s, truly I say to you, he will certainly not lose his reward.
And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it is better for him if a great millstone is hung around his neck and he has been thrown into the sea.
And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life maimed than, having two hands, to go away into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.

cmp.note: 原文是「欣嫩谷」，耶路撒冷城南的一条山谷；旧约说那里曾有人烧死儿女献祭，后来这个地名成了恶人最后受罚之处的代称。白话和和合本写「地狱」，英文照音写 Gehenna。
cmp.en: The Greek is "Gehenna," the Valley of Hinnom south of Jerusalem. The Old Testament says children were once burned there as sacrifices, and the name later came to stand for the place where the wicked are finally punished. Both Chinese versions write 地狱 (dìyù, "hell"); the English keeps the name.

verses.en: (This verse is not in the Greek edition this site follows.)

cmp.note: 较晚的抄本在第 44 节有一句和第 48 节一模一样的话（「在那里，他们的虫不死，火也不灭」）。最早的几份抄本只在第 48 节有，一般认为这里是抄写的人照第 48 节重复补上的，所以底本不收。和合本也没有这句话：它为了凑节号，把第 43 节拆成了两节；本站把那两半并回第 43 节，所以这一节的和合本栏是空的。
cmp.en: Later manuscripts have at verse 44 a sentence identical to verse 48 ("where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched"). The earliest manuscripts have it only at verse 48, and it is generally thought that copyists repeated it here, so the edition leaves it out. The Union Version does not have the sentence either: to keep the numbering it splits verse 43 in two. This site joins the two halves back under verse 43, so nothing from it is shown beside this verse.

verses.en: And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life lame than, having two feet, to be thrown into Gehenna.
(This verse is not in the Greek edition this site follows.)

cmp.note: 较晚的抄本在第 46 节有一句和第 48 节一模一样的话（「在那里，他们的虫不死，火也不灭」）。最早的几份抄本只在第 48 节有，一般认为这里是抄写的人照第 48 节重复补上的，所以底本不收。和合本也没有这句话：它为了凑节号，把第 45 节拆成了两节；本站把那两半并回第 45 节，所以这一节的和合本栏是空的。
cmp.en: Later manuscripts have at verse 46 a sentence identical to verse 48 ("where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched"). The earliest manuscripts have it only at verse 48, and it is generally thought that copyists repeated it here, so the edition leaves it out. The Union Version does not have the sentence either: to keep the numbering it splits verse 45 in two. This site joins the two halves back under verse 45, so nothing from it is shown beside this verse.

verses.en: And if your eye causes you to stumble, throw it out; it is better for you to enter the kingdom of God one-eyed than, having two eyes, to be thrown into Gehenna,
where ‘their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.’

cmp.note: 这句话引自旧约《以赛亚书》的最后一节（66:24），那里说的是背叛上帝的人的尸首。
cmp.en: The sentence is quoted from the last verse of Isaiah (66:24), where it describes the corpses of those who rebelled against God.

verses.en: For everyone will be salted with fire.
Salt is good; but if the salt becomes unsalty, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”

chapters.title: Chapter 10 · On the Road to Jerusalem
chapters.intro: Jesus heads south, teaching as he goes. Asked whether a man may divorce his wife, he answers that what God has joined no one should separate; he takes children in his arms and blesses them; a rich man who cannot bring himself to sell his possessions goes away grieving. For the third time Jesus foretells his death and rising. James and John nevertheless ask for the seats beside him, and he says that whoever would be great must be a servant. Leaving Jericho, he gives sight to the blind beggar Bartimaeus.

verses.en: And getting up from there he comes into the region of Judea and beyond the Jordan, and crowds again gather to him, and as was his custom he was again teaching them.
And they were asking him whether it is lawful for a husband to divorce a wife, testing him.
But he answered and said to them, “What did Moses command you?”
And they said, “Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of divorce and to send her away.”

cmp.note: 「休书」的规定在旧约《申命记》24:1：丈夫写一张字据交给妻子，就算离了婚。
cmp.en: The rule about a "certificate of divorce" is in Deuteronomy 24:1: a husband writes a document, hands it to his wife, and the marriage is ended.

verses.en: But Jesus said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart he wrote you this commandment;
but from the beginning of creation, ‘male and female he made them;’

cmp.note: 这一节引旧约《创世记》1:27，下面两节引《创世记》2:24。原文没有写「上帝」，只说「他造」。
cmp.en: This verse quotes Genesis 1:27, and the next two quote Genesis 2:24. The Greek does not name God here; it says only "he made."

verses.en: ‘for this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife,
and the two will become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two but one flesh.
What therefore God has joined together, let man not separate.”
And in the house again the disciples were asking him about this.
And he says to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her;
and if she, having divorced her husband, marries another, she commits adultery.”
And they were bringing little children to him so that he might touch them; but the disciples rebuked them.
But seeing it, Jesus was indignant and said to them, “Let the little children come to me; do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
Truly I say to you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will certainly not enter it.”
And taking them in his arms, he was blessing them, laying his hands on them.
And as he was going out onto the road, one man ran up and knelt before him and was asking him, “Good Teacher, what shall I do so that I may inherit eternal life?”
But Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one, God.
You know the commandments: ‘Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal, do not bear false witness, do not defraud, honor your father and mother.’”

cmp.note: 这几条出自「十诫」（旧约《出埃及记》20:12–16）。其中「不可骗取别人的东西」不在十诫原来的条文里，是这里多出来的一条。
cmp.en: These come from the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:12–16). "Do not defraud" is not among the original ten; it is an extra item in this list.

verses.en: And he said to him, “Teacher, all these I have kept from my youth.”
And Jesus, looking at him, loved him and said to him, “One thing you lack: go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”
But he, becoming gloomy at the word, went away grieving, for he had many possessions.
And looking around, Jesus says to his disciples, “How hard it will be for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!”
And the disciples were amazed at his words. But Jesus answers again and says to them, “Children, how hard it is to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
And they were exceedingly astonished, saying to one another, “Then who can be saved?”
Looking at them, Jesus says, “With men it is impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God.”
Peter began to say to him, “Look, we have left everything and have followed you.”
Jesus said, “Truly I say to you, there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or mother or father or children or fields for my sake and for the sake of the gospel,
who will not receive a hundredfold now in this time, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and fields, with persecutions, and in the age to come eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

Now they were on the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going ahead of them, and they were amazed, and those who followed were afraid. And taking the twelve aside again, he began to tell them the things that were about to happen to him:
“Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles,
and they will mock him and spit on him and flog him and kill him, and after three days he will rise.”
And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come up to him, saying to him, “Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask of you.”
And he said to them, “What do you want me to do for you?”
And they said to him, “Grant us that we may sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your glory.”
But Jesus said to them, “You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, or to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?”
And they said to him, “We are able.” And Jesus said to them, “The cup that I drink you will drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you will be baptized,
but to sit at my right or at my left is not mine to give, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared.”
And hearing it, the ten began to be indignant about James and John.
And calling them to him, Jesus says to them, “You know that those who are regarded as ruling the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
But it is not so among you; rather, whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant,
and whoever wants to be first among you shall be slave of all.
For even the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
And they come to Jericho. And as he was going out from Jericho with his disciples and a considerable crowd, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was sitting beside the road.

cmp.note: 「巴底买」是亚兰话，本身就是「底买的儿子」的意思；马可把名字和它的意思都写了出来。
cmp.en: "Bartimaeus" is Aramaic and itself means "son of Timaeus"; Mark gives both the name and its meaning.

verses.en: And hearing that it is Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say, “Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me!”
And many were rebuking him to be silent; but he was crying out all the more, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
And Jesus stopped and said, “Call him.” And they call the blind man, saying to him, “Take courage, get up; he is calling you.”
And throwing off his cloak, he jumped up and came to Jesus.
And Jesus answered him and said, “What do you want me to do for you?” And the blind man said to him, “Rabbouni, that I may see again.”
And Jesus said to him, “Go; your faith has saved you.” And immediately he saw again, and he was following him on the road.

chapters.title: Chapter 11 · Entering Jerusalem
chapters.intro: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a colt while people spread their cloaks on the road and shout “Hosanna.” The next day he curses a fig tree that has only leaves, then drives the traders out of the temple, and the chief priests and scribes begin looking for a way to destroy him. When the tree is found withered, he teaches the disciples about faith and forgiveness. The chief priests, scribes and elders demand to know by what authority he acts; he asks them in return where John’s baptism came from, and they cannot answer.

verses.en: And when they draw near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, he sends two of his disciples
and says to them, “Go into the village opposite you, and immediately as you enter it you will find a colt tied, on which no one has ever yet sat; untie it and bring it.

cmp.note: 原文只说「一匹小牲口」，没有说是驴还是马。和合本写「驴驹」，是照《马太福音》21 章讲同一件事时的说法；白话跟和合本，英文写 colt。
cmp.en: The Greek says only "a colt," a young animal, without specifying donkey or horse. The Union Version writes 驴驹 (lǘjū, "donkey colt"), following Matthew 21’s account of the same event; the plain Chinese follows it, and the English writes "colt."

verses.en: And if anyone says to you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say, ‘The Lord has need of it, and immediately he sends it back here again.’”

cmp.note: 底本这半句是门徒要说的话的一部分：主用完了马上把它送回来。和合本所据的抄本没有「回」字，译成「那人必立时让你们牵来」，成了讲那个人的反应。
cmp.en: In this edition the clause is part of what the disciples are to say: the Lord will send the animal back at once. The manuscripts behind the Union Version lack "back," and it renders 那人必立时让你们牵来 (nà rén bì lìshí ràng nǐmen qiān lái, "that person will at once let you lead it here"), making it a statement about the bystander.

verses.en: And they went away and found a colt tied at a door, outside on the street, and they untie it.
And some of those standing there were saying to them, “What are you doing, untying the colt?”
And they told them just as Jesus had said, and they let them go.
And they bring the colt to Jesus and throw their cloaks on it, and he sat on it.
And many spread their cloaks on the road, and others leafy branches, having cut them from the fields.
And those going ahead and those following were crying out, “Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!

cmp.note: 希伯来话，原意是「求你拯救」，后来成了节日里欢呼的话。这一节的话出自旧约《诗篇》118:25–26，是朝圣的人上耶路撒冷过节时唱的。
cmp.en: A Hebrew word that originally meant "save, please" and became a festival shout of praise. The words in this verse come from Psalm 118:25–26, sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem for the festivals.

verses.en: Blessed is the coming kingdom of our father David! Hosanna in the highest!”
And he entered Jerusalem, into the temple; and having looked around at everything, since the hour was already late, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
And on the next day, when they had come out from Bethany, he was hungry.
And seeing from a distance a fig tree having leaves, he came to see if perhaps he would find anything on it; and coming to it, he found nothing but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.
And he answered and said to it, “May no one ever eat fruit from you again.” And his disciples were listening.

And they come to Jerusalem. And entering the temple, he began to drive out those who were selling and those who were buying in the temple, and he overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling the doves,

cmp.note: 圣殿的外院里有买卖，是因为来献祭的人要在这里买祭牲（鸽子是穷人献的祭物），外地来的人还要把手里的钱换成圣殿肯收的钱币。
cmp.en: There was trade in the outer court of the temple because worshipers bought animals for sacrifice there (doves were the offering of the poor), and those from abroad had to change their money into the coinage the temple accepted.

verses.en: and he would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple.
And he was teaching and saying to them, “Is it not written, ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations’? But you have made it a den of robbers.”

cmp.note: 前一句引旧约《以赛亚书》56:7，「强盗窝」出自《耶利米书》7:11。原文是「强盗」，和合本写「贼窝」。
cmp.en: The first sentence quotes Isaiah 56:7; "den of robbers" comes from Jeremiah 7:11. The Greek word means "robbers" or "bandits"; the Union Version has 贼窝 (zéi wō, "den of thieves").

verses.en: And the chief priests and the scribes heard it and were seeking how they might destroy him; for they feared him, because all the crowd was astonished at his teaching.
And whenever evening came, they would go out of the city.
And passing by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots.
And Peter, remembering, says to him, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree that you cursed has withered.”
And Jesus answers and says to them, “Have faith in God.
Truly I say to you that whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be taken up and thrown into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart but believes that what he says is happening, it will be so for him.
Therefore I say to you, all things whatever you pray and ask for, believe that you have received them, and it will be so for you.
And whenever you stand praying, forgive, if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father who is in the heavens may also forgive you your trespasses.”
(This verse is not in the Greek edition this site follows.)

cmp.note: 较晚的抄本这里有一句话，意思是：你们要是不饶恕别人，天上的父也不饶恕你们的过错。和合本有这一节。这句话和《马太福音》6:15 几乎一样，最早的几份抄本没有，一般认为是抄写的人从那里补进来的，所以底本不收。
cmp.en: Later manuscripts have a sentence here meaning: if you do not forgive others, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your trespasses. The Union Version includes it. It is almost identical to Matthew 6:15 and is missing from the earliest manuscripts, so it is generally thought that copyists added it from there, and the edition leaves it out.

verses.en: And they come again to Jerusalem. And as he was walking in the temple, the chief priests and the scribes and the elders come to him
and they were saying to him, “By what authority are you doing these things? Or who gave you this authority to do these things?”
But Jesus said to them, “I will ask you one thing; answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
The baptism of John, was it from heaven or from men? Answer me.”
And they were reasoning among themselves, saying, “What should we say? If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
But should we say, ‘From men’?”—they were afraid of the crowd, for everyone held that John really was a prophet.
And answering Jesus, they say, “We do not know.” And Jesus says to them, “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.”

chapters.title: Chapter 12 · The Vineyard Tenants; Questions in the Temple
chapters.intro: Jesus is in the temple in Jerusalem. He tells a story about tenants who kill the son of the vineyard’s owner, and his hearers know it is aimed at them. Then one group after another comes with a hard question: whether to pay tax to Caesar, whose wife a woman will be when the dead rise, which commandment comes first. At the end he praises a poor widow for the two small coins she gives. “They” at the start are the chief priests, scribes and elders of the previous chapter.

verses.en: And he began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard, and put a fence around it, and dug a pit for the winepress, and built a tower, and leased it to tenant farmers, and went away on a journey.

cmp.note: 栽葡萄园、围篱笆、挖榨酒池、盖楼，这几样是照着旧约《以赛亚书》5:1–2 的话说的，那里用葡萄园比以色列民。听的人一听就知道这个故事在说谁。
cmp.en: Planting a vineyard, fencing it, digging a winepress and building a tower echo Isaiah 5:1–2, where the vineyard stands for the people of Israel; the hearers would recognize at once whom the story is about.

verses.en: And at the season he sent a slave to the tenants, to receive from the tenants some of the fruit of the vineyard.
And they took him and beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
And again he sent to them another slave; and that one they struck on the head and treated shamefully.
And he sent another, and that one they killed; and many others, beating some and killing others.
He had still one, a beloved son; he sent him last to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
But those tenants said to one another, ‘This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
And they took him and killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
What will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the tenants, and give the vineyard to others.
Have you not even read this scripture: ‘The stone that the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner;

cmp.note: 这两节引的是旧约《诗篇》118:22–23。「房角的头」指房角上最要紧的那块石头，和合本作「房角的头块石头」。
cmp.en: These two verses quote Psalm 118:22–23. "Head of the corner" is the most important stone at the corner of a building; the Union Version has 房角的头块石头 (fángjiǎo de tóu kuài shítou, "the head stone of the corner").

verses.en: this came from the Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes’?”
And they were seeking to seize him, and they feared the crowd, for they knew that he had told the parable against them. And they left him and went away.
And they send to him some of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, to trap him in a word.

And they come and say to him, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and that you care about no one, for you do not look at people’s faces, but teach the way of God in truth. Is it permitted to pay the tax to Caesar or not? Should we pay, or should we not pay?”

cmp.note: 原文是从拉丁文借来的词，指罗马向被统治的人按人头收的税。交这种税，等于承认罗马的统治，所以这个问题怎么答都会得罪一方。
cmp.en: The Greek word is borrowed from Latin (census) and means the poll tax Rome levied on its subjects. Paying it meant acknowledging Roman rule, so either answer would offend someone.

verses.en: But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them, “Why are you testing me? Bring me a denarius so that I may see it.”
And they brought one. And he says to them, “Whose image is this, and whose inscription?” And they said to him, “Caesar’s.”
And Jesus said to them, “The things of Caesar give back to Caesar, and the things of God to God.” And they were amazed at him.
And Sadducees come to him, who say there is no resurrection, and they were questioning him, saying,
“Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if someone’s brother dies and leaves behind a wife and leaves no child, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.

cmp.note: 这条规定在旧约《申命记》25:5–6：兄弟死了没有儿子，活着的兄弟要娶寡嫂，生的头一个儿子算在死者名下。
cmp.en: The rule is in Deuteronomy 25:5–6: when a man dies without a son, his brother is to marry the widow, and their first son is counted as the dead man’s.

verses.en: There were seven brothers; and the first took a wife, and when he died he left no offspring.
And the second took her, and died leaving no offspring; and the third likewise.
And the seven left no offspring. Last of all the woman also died.
In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? For the seven had her as wife.”
