Jesus said to them, “Is it not for this reason that you are mistaken, that you know neither the scriptures nor the power of God?
For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in the heavens.

But concerning the dead, that they are raised, have you not read in the book of Moses, at the passage about the bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob’?

cmp.note: 字面是「在荆棘那里」。当时经书还没有分章分节，引经文就说「讲荆棘的那一段」，指旧约《出埃及记》第 3 章：上帝在烧着却没有烧毁的荆棘里对摩西说话。引的这句话在 3:6。
cmp.en: Literally "at the bush." Scripture had no chapter or verse numbers then, so a passage was cited by its subject: "the bush" is Exodus 3, where God speaks to Moses from a bush that burns without being consumed. The words quoted are from 3:6.

verses.en: He is not God of the dead but of the living. You are greatly mistaken.”
And one of the scribes came up and heard them disputing, and seeing that he answered them well, asked him, “Which commandment is first of all?”
Jesus answered, “The first is, ‘Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one,

cmp.note: 这两节引的是旧约《申命记》6:4–5，犹太人每天早晚都要念的一段话。
cmp.en: These two verses quote Deuteronomy 6:4–5, words that Jews recite every morning and evening.

verses.en: and you shall love the Lord your God from your whole heart and from your whole soul and from your whole mind and from your whole strength.’
The second is this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”

cmp.note: 这一句引的是旧约《利未记》19:18。原文是「你身边的人」，和合本译成「爱人如己」，没有把「邻人」译出来。
cmp.en: This quotes Leviticus 19:18. The Greek is "the one near you"; the Union Version’s 爱人如己 (ài rén rú jǐ, "love people as yourself") leaves "neighbor" untranslated.

verses.en: And the scribe said to him, “Well said, Teacher; in truth you have said that he is one, and there is no other besides him;

and to love him from the whole heart and from the whole understanding and from the whole strength, and to love the neighbor as oneself, is much more than all the whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
And Jesus, seeing that he answered thoughtfully, said to him, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared to question him any longer.
And Jesus answered and said, as he taught in the temple, “How do the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
David himself said in the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet.’

cmp.note: 引的是旧约《诗篇》110:1，传统上说是大卫写的。头一个「主」指上帝，第二个「主」指上帝要立的那位王。本站的底本是「放在你的脚下」；和合本的「作你的脚凳」跟的是另一种抄本的读法，也是《诗篇》原来的说法。
cmp.en: The quotation is Psalm 110:1, traditionally ascribed to David. The first "Lord" is God, the second the king whom God will set up. The edition this site follows reads "under your feet"; the Union Version’s 作你的脚凳 (zuò nǐ de jiǎodèng, "make them your footstool") follows another manuscript reading, which is also the wording of the psalm itself.

verses.en: David himself calls him Lord; so how is he his son?” And the large crowd was listening to him gladly.
And in his teaching he was saying, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes, and like greetings in the marketplaces
and the first seats in the synagogues and the first places at the dinners,
who devour the houses of widows and for a pretense pray at length. These will receive a greater judgment.”
And sitting down opposite the treasury, he was watching how the crowd puts money into the treasury; and many rich people were putting in much.
And one poor widow came and put in two lepta, which is a quadrans.

cmp.note: 原文是「两个 lepton，就是一个 kodrantēs」。lepton 是当地最小的铜钱；作者怕读者不认识，用罗马的小钱 quadrans 换算了一下，一个 quadrans 是一个银币（一天工钱）的六十四分之一。和合本作「两个小钱，就是一个大钱」。
cmp.en: The Greek says "two lepta, which is a kodrantēs." The lepton was the smallest local copper coin; for readers who did not know it the author converts it into the Roman quadrans, one sixty-fourth of a denarius (a day’s wage). The Union Version has 两个小钱，就是一个大钱 (liǎng gè xiǎoqián, jiùshì yí gè dàqián, "two small coins, that is, one large coin").

verses.en: And calling his disciples to him, he said to them, “Amen, I say to you, this poor widow has put in more than all those putting into the treasury;
for they all put in out of their abundance, but she out of her lack put in everything she had, her whole living.”

chapters.title: Chapter 13 · The Temple’s Fall Foretold; Keep Awake
chapters.intro: Leaving the temple, Jesus says that not one of its stones will be left on another. Four disciples ask him privately when this will happen and what the sign will be. His long answer speaks of wars, persecution and a great tribulation, warns them not to be led astray by pretenders, and says that afterward the Son of Man will come in clouds. No one knows the day, so they must keep awake. From verse 5 to the end Jesus is the only speaker.

verses.en: And as he was going out of the temple, one of his disciples says to him, “Teacher, look, what stones and what buildings!”
And Jesus said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? There will not be left here a stone upon a stone that will not be thrown down.”
And as he was sitting on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew were asking him privately,
“Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign when all these things are about to be accomplished?”
And Jesus began to say to them, “See that no one leads you astray.
Many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and they will lead many astray.
And when you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be alarmed; it must happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom; there will be earthquakes in various places; there will be famines. These are the beginning of birth pains.

cmp.note: 原文是「产痛的开头」，就是女人临产时一阵阵的痛：痛是真的，但后面还有。和合本作「灾难的起头」，没有把这个比方译出来。
cmp.en: The Greek is "the beginning of birth pains," the pangs of a woman in labor: real pain, with more still to come. The Union Version has 灾难的起头 (zāinàn de qǐtóu, "the beginning of disasters") and drops the image.

verses.en: But you, watch yourselves. They will hand you over to councils, and you will be beaten in synagogues, and you will stand before governors and kings for my sake, as a testimony to them.
And the good news must first be proclaimed to all the nations.

And when they lead you away, handing you over, do not worry beforehand about what you will say, but whatever is given to you in that hour, say that; for it is not you who are speaking, but the Holy Spirit.
And brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child, and children will rise against parents and have them put to death.
And you will be hated by all because of my name. But the one who endures to the end, this one will be saved.
But when you see the abomination of desolation standing where he must not—let the reader understand—then let those in Judea flee to the mountains,

cmp.note: 这个说法出自旧约《但以理书》（9:27、11:31、12:11），一般认为那里指的是公元前二世纪外族君王在耶路撒冷圣殿里设异教祭坛的事。经文没有说明这里指什么，只插了一句「读的人要明白」；这一句是原文就有的，所以本站没有放进圆括号。
cmp.en: The phrase comes from Daniel (9:27; 11:31; 12:11), where it is generally taken to refer to a foreign king setting up a pagan altar in the Jerusalem temple in the second century BCE. The text does not say what it refers to here and only inserts "let the reader understand"; those words are part of the Greek, not an addition by this site.

verses.en: let the one on the housetop not come down or go in to take anything out of his house,
and let the one in the field not turn back to take his cloak.
But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!
And pray that it may not happen in winter.
For those days will be a tribulation such as has not been from the beginning of the creation that God created until now, and never will be.
And if the Lord had not cut short the days, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the chosen whom he chose, he cut short the days.
And then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ ‘Look, there!’ do not believe it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise and will give signs and wonders, to lead astray, if possible, the chosen.
But you, watch; I have told you everything beforehand.
But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light,

cmp.note: 太阳变黑、月亮无光、星星坠落，是旧约先知书里讲上帝审判时常用的说法（如《以赛亚书》13:10、34:4）。
cmp.en: The darkened sun, the lightless moon and the falling stars are stock language in the Old Testament prophets for God’s judgment (for example Isaiah 13:10; 34:4).

verses.en: and the stars will be falling from heaven, and the powers in the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory.

cmp.w: ton huion tou anthrōpou erchomenon en nephelais
cmp.note: 这句话照着旧约《但以理书》7:13 说的：那里说「有一位像人子的，驾着天上的云而来」，从上帝那里得了权柄和国度。
cmp.en: The sentence follows Daniel 7:13, where "one like a son of man" comes with the clouds of heaven and receives authority and a kingdom from God.

verses.en: And then he will send out the angels and gather the chosen from the four winds, from the end of the earth to the end of heaven.
From the fig tree learn the parable: when its branch has already become tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
So also you, when you see these things happening, know that he is near, at the doors.

cmp.note: 原文只有「近了」，没有主语，可以读成「他近了」，也可以读成「那事近了」。白话和英文都取了前一种。
cmp.en: The Greek says only "is near," with no subject; it can be read "he is near" or "it is near." Both translations here take the first.

verses.en: Amen, I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But concerning that day or the hour, no one knows, neither the angels in heaven nor the Son, only the Father.
Watch, stay awake; for you do not know when the time is.
It is like a man away on a journey, who left his house and gave authority to his slaves, to each his work, and commanded the doorkeeper to keep awake.
So keep awake, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming, whether in the evening or at midnight or at cockcrow or early in the morning,

cmp.w: opse ē mesonyktion ē alektorophōnias ē prōï
cmp.note: 傍晚、半夜、鸡叫、清早，是罗马人把一夜分成的四段（四更）。
cmp.en: Evening, midnight, cockcrow and early morning are the four watches into which the Romans divided the night.

verses.en: lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.
And what I say to you I say to all: keep awake.”

chapters.title: Chapter 14 · The Last Supper, the Arrest, the Trial
chapters.intro: Two days before Passover the chief priests are looking for a way to get rid of Jesus quietly, and Judas, one of his own disciples, agrees to hand him over. A woman pours costly ointment on his head. Jesus eats the Passover meal with the twelve and speaks of the bread and the cup as his body and his blood. That night he prays in Gethsemane, is arrested, and is tried before the council, which finds him deserving of death; meanwhile Peter says three times that he does not know him.

verses.en: Now it was the Passover and the Unleavened Bread after two days. And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how to seize him by deceit and kill him,
for they said, “Not during the festival, lest there be an uproar of the people.”

And while he was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, as he was reclining at table, a woman came having an alabaster jar of ointment of pure nard, very costly; breaking the jar, she poured it over his head.
But there were some who were indignant among themselves: “Why has this waste of the ointment happened?
For this ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor.” And they were scolding her.
But Jesus said, “Leave her alone; why do you cause her trouble? She has done a good work on me.
For you always have the poor with you, and whenever you want you can do good to them; but me you do not always have.
She did what she could; she anointed my body beforehand for burial.
And amen, I say to you, wherever the good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”
And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went off to the chief priests in order to hand him over to them.
And when they heard it they were glad, and promised to give him silver. And he was seeking how to hand him over at a good moment.
And on the first day of the Unleavened Bread, when they sacrificed the Passover lamb, his disciples say to him, “Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover?”
And he sends two of his disciples and says to them, “Go into the city, and a man carrying a jar of water will meet you; follow him,
and wherever he enters, say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says: Where is my guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’
And he will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready; and there prepare for us.”
And the disciples went out and came into the city and found it just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
And when evening came, he comes with the twelve.
And as they were reclining and eating, Jesus said, “Amen, I say to you, one of you will hand me over, one who is eating with me.”

cmp.note: 原文是「交出去」，和合本在这一章都译成「卖」。这个动词在这卷书里一再出现：约翰「被交出去」（1:14），人子要「被交到人手里」（9:31），这里是犹大把耶稣「交出去」。
cmp.en: The Greek is "hand over," which the Union Version renders throughout this chapter as 卖 (mài, "sell," that is, betray). The verb runs through the book: John is "handed over" (1:14), the Son of Man is to be "handed over" into human hands (9:31), and here Judas "hands over" Jesus.

verses.en: They began to be grieved and to say to him one by one, “Surely not I?”
And he said to them, “One of the twelve, the one dipping with me into the bowl.
For the Son of Man goes as it is written about him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would be better for him if that man had not been born.”
And as they were eating, he took bread, and having blessed it he broke it and gave it to them and said, “Take; this is my body.”
And taking a cup, having given thanks he gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
And he said to them, “This is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many.
Amen, I say to you, I will no longer drink of the fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.”
And having sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
And Jesus says to them, “You will all fall away, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.’

cmp.note: 引的是旧约《撒迦利亚书》13:7。
cmp.en: The quotation is from Zechariah 13:7.

verses.en: But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”
But Peter said to him, “Even if all fall away, yet I will not.”
And Jesus says to him, “Amen, I say to you that you, today, this very night, before a rooster crows twice, will deny me three times.”
But he kept saying vehemently, “If I must die with you, I will not deny you.” And they all said the same.
And they come to a place whose name is Gethsemane, and he says to his disciples, “Sit here while I pray.”
And he takes Peter and James and John with him, and he began to be greatly distressed and troubled,
and he says to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, to the point of death; remain here and keep awake.”
And going a little farther, he fell on the ground and was praying that, if it were possible, the hour might pass from him,
and he was saying, “Abba, Father, all things are possible for you; take this cup away from me; yet not what I will, but what you will.”

cmp.note: abba 是亚兰话的「父亲」。亚兰话是耶稣和当地人平常说的话；经文先照着他的原话写一遍，再用希腊文说一遍「父」。
cmp.en: Abba is Aramaic for "father." Aramaic was the everyday language of Jesus and the people around him; the text first gives his own word and then repeats it in Greek.

verses.en: And he comes and finds them sleeping, and he says to Peter, “Simon, are you sleeping? Were you not strong enough to keep awake one hour?
Keep awake and pray, that you may not come into testing; the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
And again he went away and prayed, saying the same words.
And again he came and found them sleeping, for their eyes were very heavy, and they did not know what to answer him.
And he comes the third time and says to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? It is enough; the hour has come. Look, the Son of Man is handed over into the hands of sinners.

cmp.note: 这一句有两处读法不一。前半句可以读成问句（「你们还在睡吗？」），也可以读成一句话（「你们继续睡吧」，和合本这样译）；白话和英文取了问句。apechei 一个词的意思不确定，通常译成「够了」。
cmp.en: Two things in this sentence are read differently. The first half can be a question ("Are you still sleeping?") or a statement ("Sleep on now," as the Union Version has it); both translations here take it as a question. The single word apechei is of uncertain meaning and is usually rendered "it is enough."

verses.en: Rise, let us go; look, the one handing me over has come near.”
And immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrives, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
Now the one handing him over had given them a signal, saying, “The one I kiss is he; seize him and lead him away securely.”
And when he came, he immediately went up to him and says, “Rabbi!” and he kissed him.
And they laid hands on him and seized him.
But a certain one of those standing by drew his sword and struck the slave of the high priest and cut off his ear.
And Jesus answered and said to them, “Have you come out as against a bandit, with swords and clubs, to capture me?
Day after day I was with you in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me. But let the scriptures be fulfilled.”
And they all left him and fled.
And a certain young man was following him, wearing a linen cloth over his naked body, and they seize him,
but he left the linen cloth behind and fled naked.
And they led Jesus away to the high priest, and all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes come together.
And Peter followed him from a distance, right into the courtyard of the high priest, and he was sitting with the attendants and warming himself at the fire.
Now the chief priests and the whole council were seeking testimony against Jesus to put him to death, and they were not finding any;
for many were giving false testimony against him, and their testimonies did not agree.
And some stood up and were giving false testimony against him, saying,
“We heard him saying, ‘I will destroy this temple made with hands, and in three days I will build another not made with hands.’”
And not even so did their testimony agree.
And the high priest stood up in the midst and questioned Jesus, saying, “Do you answer nothing? What is it that these men testify against you?”
But he was silent and answered nothing. Again the high priest was questioning him and says to him, “Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?”

cmp.note: 犹太人为了表示敬畏，不直接说「上帝」，用别的说法代替：这一节的「那当受称颂者」，下一节的「那权能者」，指的都是上帝。
cmp.en: Out of reverence Jews avoided saying "God" directly and used substitutes: "the Blessed One" in this verse and "the Power" in the next both mean God.

verses.en: And Jesus said, “I am; and you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Power and coming with the clouds of heaven.”

cmp.w: ek dexiōn kathēmenon … meta tōn nephelōn
cmp.note: 这句话把旧约的两处合在一起：《诗篇》110:1「你坐在我的右边」，和《但以理书》7:13「有一位像人子的，驾着天上的云而来」。
cmp.en: The sentence joins two Old Testament passages: Psalm 110:1, "Sit at my right hand," and Daniel 7:13, "one like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven."

verses.en: And the high priest, tearing his garments, says, “What further need do we have of witnesses?
You have heard the blasphemy. How does it appear to you?” And they all condemned him as deserving death.
And some began to spit on him and to cover his face and to strike him with their fists and to say to him, “Prophesy!” And the attendants received him with slaps.
And while Peter was below in the courtyard, one of the servant girls of the high priest comes,
and seeing Peter warming himself, she looked at him and says, “You also were with the Nazarene, Jesus.”
But he denied it, saying, “I neither know nor understand what you are saying.” And he went out into the forecourt, and a rooster crowed.
And the servant girl, seeing him, began again to say to those standing by, “This man is one of them.”
But again he denied it. And after a little while those standing by again said to Peter, “Truly you are one of them, for you are a Galilean, and your speech is like it.”
But he began to curse and to swear, “I do not know this man you are talking about.”
And immediately a rooster crowed a second time. And Peter remembered the word, how Jesus had said to him, “Before a rooster crows twice, you will deny me three times.” And he broke down and wept.

cmp.note: 这个词在这里是什么意思不确定：可以是「想到这里」（和合本「思想起来」，白话也这样译），也可以是「忍不住」「冲出去」。英文取了「忍不住」。
cmp.en: What this word means here is uncertain: it may be "thinking on it" (so the Union Version’s 思想起来, sīxiǎng qǐlái, "when he thought on it," and the Chinese here), or "breaking down," or "rushing out." The English here takes "broke down."

chapters.title: Chapter 15 · Before Pilate; the Crucifixion and Burial
chapters.intro: Early in the morning the council hands Jesus over to Pilate, the Roman governor. Pilate is inclined to release him, but the crowd asks for Barabbas instead and demands that Jesus be crucified. After the soldiers have mocked him, he is crucified at Golgotha with a bandit on either side. From noon darkness covers the land, and at three in the afternoon he gives a loud cry and dies. That evening Joseph of Arimathea lays him in a tomb cut out of rock.

verses.en: And immediately, early in the morning, the chief priests held a consultation with the elders and scribes and the whole council, and having bound Jesus they led him away and handed him over to Pilate.
And Pilate questioned him, “Are you the King of the Jews?” And answering him he says, “You say so.”

cmp.note: 字面是「你说」，既没有直接承认，也没有否认。和合本译成「你说的是」，听起来像是承认了。
cmp.en: Literally "You say," neither a plain yes nor a denial. The Union Version’s 你说的是 (nǐ shuō de shì, "what you say is so") sounds like an affirmation.

verses.en: And the chief priests were accusing him of many things.
And Pilate again was questioning him, saying, “Do you answer nothing? See how many things they accuse you of.”
But Jesus no longer answered anything, so that Pilate was amazed.
Now at the festival he used to release for them one prisoner whom they requested.
And there was the one called Barabbas, bound with the insurrectionists who had committed murder in the insurrection.
And the crowd came up and began to ask him to do as he used to do for them.
And Pilate answered them, saying, “Do you want me to release for you the King of the Jews?”
For he knew that it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed him over.
But the chief priests stirred up the crowd so that he would rather release Barabbas for them.
And Pilate again answered and was saying to them, “What then do you want me to do with the one you call the King of the Jews?”
And they cried out again, “Crucify him!”
And Pilate was saying to them, “Why, what evil has he done?” But they cried out all the more, “Crucify him!”
And Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas for them, and having had Jesus flogged, he handed him over to be crucified.
And the soldiers led him away inside the courtyard, that is, the praetorium, and they call together the whole cohort.
And they clothe him in purple, and having woven a crown of thorns they put it on him;
and they began to salute him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”
And they were striking his head with a reed and spitting on him, and kneeling down they were paying homage to him.
And when they had mocked him, they stripped him of the purple and put his own clothes on him. And they lead him out to crucify him.
And they compel a certain passerby, Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.
And they bring him to the place Golgotha, which is translated, Place of a Skull.
And they were giving him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not take it.
And they crucify him, and they divide his garments, casting lots for them, who should take what.

cmp.note: 分衣服、抽签，用的是旧约《诗篇》22:18 的话：「他们分我的外衣，为我的里衣抽签。」这一章后面耶稣喊的那一句（第 34 节）出自同一篇诗的第一句。
cmp.en: The dividing of the garments by lot uses the words of Psalm 22:18: "They divide my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots." The cry of Jesus later in this chapter (verse 34) is the opening line of the same psalm.

verses.en: Now it was the third hour, and they crucified him.
And the inscription of the charge against him was written: “The King of the Jews.”
And with him they crucify two bandits, one on his right and one on his left.
(This verse is not in the Greek edition this site follows.)

cmp.note: 较晚的抄本在这里有一句话，说这就应验了经上「他被算在不法的人当中」的话（引的是旧约《以赛亚书》53:12；《路加福音》22:37 也引了这一句）。最早的几份抄本都没有这一节，一般认为是后来的抄写者加进来的，所以校勘本不收。节号照旧留着，后面各节的编号才不会变。
cmp.en: Later manuscripts have a sentence here saying that this fulfilled the scripture "he was counted among the lawless" (Isaiah 53:12, which Luke 22:37 also quotes). The earliest manuscripts do not have the verse, and it is generally thought to have been added by later copyists, so critical editions leave it out. The number is kept so that the verses after it are not renumbered.

verses.en: And those passing by were reviling him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who destroy the temple and build it in three days,
save yourself by coming down from the cross!”
Likewise also the chief priests, mocking among themselves with the scribes, were saying, “He saved others; himself he cannot save.
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, that we may see and believe.” And those crucified with him were reviling him.
And when the sixth hour came, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which is translated, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”

cmp.note: 这是亚兰话，耶稣和当地人平常说的话；经文先照着原话的读音写下来，再翻成希腊文。这句话是旧约《诗篇》第 22 篇的第一句。
cmp.en: This is Aramaic, the everyday language of Jesus and the people around him; the text first writes out the sound of his words and then translates them into Greek. The sentence is the first line of Psalm 22.

verses.en: And some of those standing by, hearing it, were saying, “Look, he is calling Elijah.”
And someone ran and, filling a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed and was giving him a drink, saying, “Wait, let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”
But Jesus, letting out a loud cry, breathed his last.
And the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.

cmp.note: 「裂开」和第 1 章第 10 节「天裂开了」是同一个动词：这卷书开头是天被撕开，结尾是圣殿的幔子被撕开。
cmp.en: "Was torn" is the same verb as in 1:10, where the heavens are torn open: the book begins with the heavens torn and ends with the temple curtain torn.

verses.en: And the centurion who stood facing him, seeing that he breathed his last in this way, said, “Truly this man was God’s Son.”
Now there were also women watching from a distance, among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome,
who, when he was in Galilee, used to follow him and serve him, and many others who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
And when evening had already come, since it was the Preparation, that is, the day before the Sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathea came, a respected member of the council, who was himself also waiting for the kingdom of God; taking courage, he went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
But Pilate wondered whether he was already dead, and summoning the centurion he asked him whether he had been dead for some time.
And when he learned it from the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.
And having bought a linen cloth, he took him down, wrapped him in the linen cloth and laid him in a tomb that had been hewn out of rock, and he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were watching where he was laid.

chapters.title: Chapter 16 · The Empty Tomb, and Two Later Endings
chapters.intro: Early on the morning after the Sabbath three women bring spices to the tomb, find the stone already rolled away, and are told by a young man in a white robe that Jesus has been raised. They run away terrified and say nothing to anyone. The earliest manuscripts end here, at verse 8; the short ending that follows and verses 9–20 are generally thought to have been added later, and are translated here as the Greek edition prints them, inside double brackets.

verses.en: And when the Sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James and Salome bought spices, so that they might come and anoint him.
And very early on the first day of the week they come to the tomb, when the sun had risen.
And they were saying to one another, “Who will roll away the stone for us from the door of the tomb?”
And looking up, they see that the stone has been rolled away; for it was very large.
And entering the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a white robe, and they were alarmed.
But he says to them, “Do not be alarmed. You are looking for Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has been raised; he is not here. See the place where they laid him.
But go, tell his disciples and Peter, ‘He is going ahead of you into Galilee; there you will see him, just as he told you.’”

And going out, they fled from the tomb, for trembling and astonishment had seized them; and they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid. ⟦But all that had been commanded they reported briefly to those around Peter. And after these things Jesus himself also sent out through them, from east to west, the sacred and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation. Amen.⟧

cmp.note: 最早的几份抄本到「因为她们害怕」就结束了。后面这一小段通常叫「短结尾」，只见于少数较晚的抄本，一般认为是后来加的；底本把它放在双方括号 ⟦ ⟧ 里，表示它不属于原来的经文。和合本没有这一段。
cmp.en: The earliest manuscripts end with "for they were afraid." The few sentences after it are usually called the shorter ending; they are found only in a small number of later manuscripts and are generally thought to be a later addition. The Greek edition prints them inside double brackets ⟦ ⟧ to mark that they are not part of the original text. The Union Version does not have them.

verses.en: ⟦Now having risen early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.

cmp.note: 第 9–20 节通常叫「长结尾」。绝大多数抄本有这一段，和合本和历来的译本也都有；但最早的几份抄本没有，用词和写法也和前面不一样，一般认为是后来有人补写的。底本把整段放在双方括号 ⟦ ⟧ 里。
cmp.en: Verses 9–20 are usually called the longer ending. The great majority of manuscripts have it, and so do the Union Version and the traditional translations; but the earliest manuscripts lack it, and its vocabulary and style differ from what comes before, so it is generally thought to have been supplied later. The Greek edition prints the whole passage inside double brackets ⟦ ⟧.

verses.en: She went and reported to those who had been with him, as they were mourning and weeping.
And they, hearing that he was alive and had been seen by her, did not believe.
And after these things he was shown in a different form to two of them as they were walking, going into the country.
And they went back and reported to the rest; neither did they believe them.

And afterward he was shown to the eleven themselves as they were reclining at table, and he reproached their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they had not believed those who saw him after he had been raised.
And he said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.
The one who believes and is baptized will be saved, but the one who does not believe will be condemned.
And these signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak in new tongues;
they will pick up snakes, and if they drink anything deadly it will not harm them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will recover.”
So then the Lord Jesus, after speaking to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
And they went out and proclaimed everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word through the accompanying signs.⟧

title: The Gospel according to Mark
summary: The shortest of the four Gospels that open the New Testament: what Jesus, whom Christians hold to be the deliverer sent by God, did and said, and how he was crucified and rose. It moves fast, one event after another. All 16 chapters are here, from his baptism in the Jordan to the empty tomb.

primer.a: 基督教的圣经分成两大部分：旧约（耶稣以前犹太人的经书）和新约（讲耶稣和最早一批信他的人）。新约开头有四卷「福音书」，各自把耶稣的事讲了一遍，《马可福音》是其中最短的一卷，一般认为也是最早写成的，大约在公元 65 到 75 年之间，用的是当时地中海一带通行的希腊文。书里没有写作者的名字；传统上说作者叫马可，是耶稣的门徒彼得身边的人。
全书是一个讲故事的人在叙述，他自己不出场。引号里的话，是故事里的人说的：耶稣、约翰、门徒、围观的人，有时是附在人身上的鬼。叙述里的「他」，大多数时候指耶稣。
故事发生在大约公元 30 年前后，地点是地中海东岸的犹太人地区（今天的以色列、巴勒斯坦一带），当时归罗马帝国管。犹太人只拜一位上帝，照着祖先摩西传下来的律法过日子：每周有一天安息日不做工，各地有会堂聚会读经，耶路撒冷有圣殿，由祭司献祭。很多人在盼望上帝派一位救主来，这位救主希伯来话叫「弥赛亚」，希腊话叫「基督」。

primer.q: 读的时候会卡住的地方
primer.a: 一是节奏很快：「立刻」这个词在第 1 章就出现了 11 次，全书 41 次，一件事刚说完就接下一件，中间不解释。二是经常引旧约的话，开头第 2、3 节就是。三是耶稣常常不许人、也不许鬼把他是谁说出去，书里没有说明原因。四是「洁净」和「不洁净」：按当时的律法，某些病、某些东西会让人不能参加敬拜、不能和别人来往，所以治病在书里常常说成「洁净了」。
这些词在书里反复出现，先认一下。
terms: 福音
字面是「好消息」。书里指耶稣带来的消息：上帝的国近了。
基督
希腊话，意思是「受膏的人」，就是上帝选立的那一位救主；希伯来话叫弥赛亚。后来成了耶稣的称号。
上帝的国
不是一块地方，而是上帝亲自作王、他的心意行得通的局面。
人子
耶稣说到自己时最常用的称呼。字面是「人的儿子」，也是旧约里一位从上帝那里得到权柄的人物的称号。
门徒
跟着耶稣学的人。其中他特别选出十二个，书里常叫「那十二个人」。
法利赛人
犹太人里严守律法和各种规矩的一派，在书里常常和耶稣争论。
安息日
每周的第七天。犹太人这一天不做工，敬拜上帝。
会堂
犹太人在各城各镇聚会、读经、祷告的地方。
文士
专门抄写、讲解犹太律法的学者。
污灵、鬼
书里说会附在人身上、让人生病或发狂的邪灵。

primer.a: 全书 16 章，从第 1 章顺着读就可以：它没有讲耶稣出生和小时候，一开头就是他出来传道。前 8 章主要在加利利，讲他治病、赶鬼、教导人；第 8 章末尾起，他三次预告自己要被杀，一路走向耶路撒冷；第 11 到 16 章是他在耶路撒冷的最后一个星期。只想先读一段的话，读第 14、15 章（被捕、受审、钉十字架）。

primerEn.q: What kind of book this is
primerEn.a: The Christian Bible has two main parts: the Old Testament (the Jewish scriptures from before Jesus) and the New Testament (about Jesus and the first people who believed in him). The New Testament opens with four "Gospels," each telling the story of Jesus. Mark is the shortest and is generally thought to be the earliest, written around 65 to 75 CE in the everyday Greek of the eastern Mediterranean. The book does not name its author; by tradition he was Mark, a companion of Jesus’s disciple Peter.

A narrator tells the whole story and never appears in it. Words in quotation marks are spoken by people in the story: Jesus, John, the disciples, the crowds, and sometimes the demons possessing a person. "He" in the narration is usually Jesus.

The story takes place around 30 CE in the Jewish lands on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean (today’s Israel and Palestine), then under the Roman Empire. Jews worshiped one God and lived by the law handed down from their ancestor Moses: a weekly Sabbath with no work, synagogues in every town for gathering and reading scripture, and a temple in Jerusalem where priests offered sacrifices. Many were waiting for God to send a deliverer, called "Messiah" in Hebrew and "Christ" in Greek.

First, the pace: the word "immediately" occurs 11 times in chapter 1 alone and 41 times in the book; one event follows another with no explanation in between. Second, the Old Testament is quoted often, starting in verses 2 and 3. Third, Jesus repeatedly forbids people and demons to say who he is, and the book does not explain why. Fourth, "clean" and "unclean": under the law of the time, certain illnesses and things barred a person from worship and from contact with others, so a healing is often described as being "made clean."
These words recur throughout the book.
terms: Good news (gospel)
In this book, the news Jesus brings: the kingdom of God has come near.
Christ
Greek for "anointed one," the deliverer chosen by God; "Messiah" in Hebrew. It later became a title for Jesus.
Kingdom of God
Not a territory but the state of affairs in which God himself rules and his will is done.
Son of Man
The name Jesus most often uses for himself. Literally "son of a human being," it is also the title of a figure in the Old Testament who receives authority from God.
Disciples
Those who follow Jesus and learn from him. He singles out twelve of them, often called simply "the Twelve."
Pharisees
A Jewish group strict about keeping the law and its many rules; in this book they often argue with Jesus.
Sabbath
The seventh day of the week, when Jews do no work and worship God.
Synagogue
The place in each town where Jews gathered to read scripture and pray.
Scribes
Scholars who copied and explained the Jewish law.
Unclean spirits, demons
Evil spirits which, the book says, take hold of people and make them ill or frenzied.

primerEn.a: The book has 16 chapters; simply read from chapter 1. It says nothing about Jesus’s birth or childhood and opens with him beginning his public work. The first eight chapters are mostly in Galilee: healings, exorcisms, teaching. From the end of chapter 8 he foretells three times that he will be killed, and travels toward Jerusalem. Chapters 11 to 16 are his last week there. If you want just one stretch, read chapters 14 and 15: the arrest, the trials and the crucifixion.

compare: 希腊文原文用 SBL Greek New Testament（SBLGNT），只去掉了底本里的校勘符号，经文本身没有动；罗马转写是本站按通行规则机械生成的，不标重音。底本里用双方括号 ⟦ ⟧ 括起来的，是编者认为后来才加进去的文字（第 16 章的两种结尾）。
白话是写给完全没接触过圣经的人看的：用平常说话的词，把谁在对谁说写清楚。原文没有、但不补就看不懂的字，一律放在圆括号（）里；括号里是通行的解释，不是经文本身。英文版贴着字面译，不加括号，两版对着看就知道哪些是补的。白话、英文和所有说明都是 AI 从希腊文译写的，没有经过圣经学者或教会审阅。
对照栏是 1919 年出版的官话和合译本（和合本），录文取自维基文库，繁体转成简体，几个异体字（汚、徧、痲、愼）改成了通行写法，原书的旧式标点照录。维基文库录的是称「神」的版本；本站的白话写「上帝」。人名、地名跟和合本走（耶稣、西门、安得烈、迦百农），只有两处用了今天更常见的写法：约旦河（和合本作「约但河」）、撒旦（和合本作「撒但」）。
和合本当年依据的希腊文底本和 SBLGNT 不完全一样，所以有的地方三栏对不上，不是译错：第 1 章第 1 节和合本多「神的儿子」；第 1 章第 41 节和合本是「动了慈心」，本站的底本是「动了怒」。有五节（7:16、9:44、9:46、11:26、15:28）底本没有、和合本有，本站留着节号，原文栏放一个「—」。这些地方都在那一节下面的「三语对照」里写明。
这卷书的希腊文很口语：句子几乎都用「然后」（kai）开头，过去的事常用现在时来讲（「他们进了迦百农」原文是「他们进迦百农」），「立刻」（euthys）一再出现。英文保留了这些；白话为了读得顺，省掉了大部分句首的「然后」，「立刻」照译。
compareEn: The Greek is the SBL Greek New Testament (SBLGNT) with its text-critical sigla removed and nothing else changed; the romanization is generated mechanically by this site under the usual conventions, without accents. Text in double square brackets ⟦ ⟧ is what the editors judge to be later additions (the two endings in chapter 16).

The Chinese is written for readers who have never opened a Bible: everyday words, with who is speaking to whom made explicit. Words that are not in the Greek but are needed to follow it are put in parentheses; they give the usual explanation and are not part of the text. The English stays close to the wording and adds no parentheses, so reading the two side by side shows what was supplied. The Chinese, the English and all the notes were translated and written by AI from the Greek and have not been reviewed by biblical scholars or by any church.

The older Chinese version shown alongside is the Mandarin Union Version of 1919, taken from Chinese Wikisource, converted to simplified characters with a few variant characters normalized and its original punctuation kept. Wikisource carries the edition that calls God 神 (Shén); this site’s plain Chinese writes 上帝 (Shàngdì). Names follow the Union Version, except for two that are now more commonly written another way: the Jordan (约旦河 Yuēdàn Hé) and Satan (撒旦 Sādàn).

The Union Version was made from a Greek text that differs in places from SBLGNT, so where the columns disagree it is not always a mistranslation: in 1:1 the Union Version adds "the Son of God," and in 1:41 it has "moved with compassion" where this site’s edition reads "being angered." Five verses (7:16; 9:44; 9:46; 11:26; 15:28) are in the Union Version but not in this edition; the verse numbers are kept, with a dash in the Greek column. Each such place is explained in the note under that verse.

Mark’s Greek is colloquial: nearly every sentence begins with "and" (kai), past events are often told in the present tense ("they go into Capernaum"), and "immediately" (euthys) keeps returning. The English keeps these; the Chinese drops most of the sentence-opening "and" to read smoothly but keeps "immediately."
